records.title: Return healthy crop residue to the soil
records.summary: After harvest, cut healthy stalks, leaves and roots and leave them on pits and beds instead of removing or burning them.
instructions: Leave roots of legumes in the soil.
Chop stalks to forearm lengths and lay them over pits and beds.
Pin them down with a few stones against wind.
everyday_amounts: all healthy residue stays on the plot
limitations: Residue may also be needed for animal feed; keep at least the pit and bed residue on the soil.
safety_notes: Do not burn residue; dry-season fires spread quickly.
records.purpose: Put organic matter back into the thin soil and keep it covered through the long dry season.
expected_observable_change: Soil under residue stays darker and softer
Termites and soil life break residue down over the dry season

records.title: Keep the soil covered through the dry season
records.summary: Keep mulch on pits and beds all through the dry period and top it up before the next rains.
instructions: Top up with dry grass, leaves and prunings whenever available.
Keep animals and fire away from the plot.
everyday_amounts: a layer about a hand's depth
limitations: Mulch disappears quickly to termites; expect to top it up.
safety_notes: Clear a firebreak around the plot.
records.purpose: Protect the surface from crusting and loss, and let soil life work.
expected_observable_change: Less crust and more soil life when rains return

records.title: Compost healthy residue and scraps
records.summary: Pile healthy residue, leaves, scraps and any manure into a compost heap or pit to fill pits next season.
instructions: Layer coarse stalks, leaves, scraps and a little soil.
Keep it damp when possible; cover with grass.
Use when dark and crumbly.
limitations: Slow in the dry season without moisture.
safety_notes: Keep compost away from wells and drinking water.
records.purpose: Build next season's main fertility input.
records.timing: After harvest and through the dry season

records.title: Remove diseased residue and striga safely
records.summary: Residue from heavily diseased plants, and all striga plants, should be taken off the plot and burned in a safe place or buried deep.
instructions: Bag striga plants before carrying them so seeds do not drop.
Burn only in a small, cleared spot away from dry grass, homes and trees, on a calm day, and watch it until it is out.
Or bury deeply far from the plot.
limitations: Striga seed in the soil lasts many years.
safety_notes: Never leave a fire unattended; keep water or sand at hand.
Do not burn near homes, trees or dry grass.
records.purpose: Stop diseases and striga seed carrying over to the next season.
expected_observable_change: Fewer diseased plants and striga next season

records.title: Extend pits and stone lines in the dry season
records.summary: Use the dry season to dig more pits in the softest spots, re-fill old pits with organic matter, and extend or repair stone lines.
instructions: Re-open last season's pits, add a bucketful or two of compost, and reuse them.
Dig new pits beside the best-performing ones.
Extend stone lines along the same contour and add new lines below.
Repair any line where water broke through.
everyday_amounts: one to two bucketfuls of compost per re-used pit
new lines a few paces apart
limitations: Labour is the limit; extend what worked, not everything.
safety_notes: Do not force tools through rock; keep away from edges.
records.purpose: Grow the improved area step by step while labour is free and before the rains.
records.timing: Dry season, before the next rains
expected_observable_change: Old pits darken and soften season by season
More soil builds behind stone lines

records.title: Expand gradually, only after the trial works
records.summary: Grow the planted area only with the crops and methods that did well in the trial.
instructions: Compare trial pits, beds and crops from your journal.
Next season, double at most the area under the best method.
Keep a small part as a new trial for one more crop or method.
everyday_amounts: at most about double the trial area each season
limitations: A single season can mislead; weigh unusual weather.
records.purpose: Avoid spending scarce seed, water and labour on untested methods.

records.title: Rotate legumes and cereals
records.summary: Next season, sow millet where legumes grew and legumes where millet grew.
instructions: Mark in the journal what grew in each pit or bed.
Swap cereal and legume places next season.
records.purpose: Spread the nitrogen benefit of legumes and break pest and striga cycles.

records.title: Plant hedges and trees along stone lines
records.summary: Plant gliricidia cuttings or tufted grasses along stone lines and bed edges, and trees such as cashew in the deepest pockets.
instructions: Plant cuttings along stone lines at the start of the rains.
Plant tree seedlings in enlarged pits in the deepest spots.
Protect young plants from animals with thorny branches.
everyday_amounts: cuttings about a pace apart along lines
limitations: Trees take years; they do not replace this season's field crops.
safety_notes: Gliricidia seeds and bark are toxic; do not eat.
records.purpose: Hold stone lines in place, add leaf litter, and build long-term options on the plateau.
expected_observable_change: Living lines hold more soil and give mulch

records.title: Save seed from the best plants
records.summary: Keep seed from the healthiest plants that did best on this ground.
instructions: Mark the best plants before harvest.
Harvest, dry and store their seed separately, labelled.
Store seed in sealed containers in a cool, dry place.
everyday_amounts: keep at least a few handfuls of each crop
limitations: Hybrid seed may not breed true.
safety_notes: Never eat seed treated with chemicals.
records.purpose: Build seed suited to this soil and season.
expected_observable_change: More reliable germination and growth over seasons

records.title: Cover crop or living mulch after harvest
records.summary: Where moisture remains after the main harvest, sow cowpea or horse gram as a cover crop so the ground is not left bare; cut it down and leave it as mulch before it competes with the next crop.
instructions: Right after the main harvest, if the soil is still moist a finger deep, sow cowpea or horse gram thinly into pits and beds between the residue.
Horse gram is the hardier choice late in the season; cowpea covers the ground faster.
Let it grow as long as moisture lasts; pick a few leaves or pods if they come.
Before the next sowing, cut it at the soil surface and lay it on the bed as mulch; leave the roots in the soil.
Where moisture is too short, keep a dead mulch of residue instead.
everyday_amounts: sow thinly: a pinch of seeds about two hand-spans apart
cut at the soil surface before the next sowing
limitations: Needs some moisture left after harvest; in a dry end of season it may not establish.
A cover crop left growing too long competes with the next crop for water.
safety_notes: Cook any dry beans thoroughly before eating.
records.purpose: Keep living cover on the soil, add nitrogen and organic matter, and shade out weeds through the end of the rains.
records.timing: Right after harvest, while soil is still moist
expected_observable_change: Next crop greener where the cover grew

records.title: Preserve beds, pits, stone lines and windbreaks between seasons
records.summary: Do not flatten or dig out what you built: keep beds, pits, stone lines, half-moons and windbreaks in place and improve them each season.
instructions: Leave raised beds standing; top them up with compost and residue rather than rebuilding.
Mark pits so they can be re-opened and refilled, not dug anew.
Repair stone lines and half-moon banks after the last storms of the season.
Keep dead hedges and live hedges in place; add brush to gaps and replant failed cuttings.
Keep animals and fire away from beds and hedges in the dry season; walking paths go between beds, never on them.
limitations: Structures need some repair every season; plan the work for the dry season.
safety_notes: Never burn hedges or residue near beds; fires spread fast on dry plateaus.
records.purpose: Each season's work adds to the last; keeping structures saves labour and keeps building soil depth.
expected_observable_change: Beds get deeper and darker over seasons
More soil collects behind stone lines each year
Hedges thicken and shelter more of the plot
